sanskrit: te tu dṛṣṭvā maheṣvāsā bhūtale patitaṃ nṛpam moham abhyāgaman sarve kṛpaprabhṛtayo rathāḥ
english: But when those great archers saw the king fallen to the earth, all the chariot-warriors, Kṛpa and the rest, were overcome with a swoon.

sanskrit: avatīrya rathebhyas tu prādravan rājasaṃnidhau duryodhanaṃ ca saṃprekṣya sarve bhūmāv upāviśan
english: Descending from their chariots, they ran to where the king lay, and gazing upon Duryodhana, they all sank down upon the ground.

sanskrit: tato drauṇir mahārāja bāṣpapūrṇekṣaṇaḥ śvasan uvāca bharataśreṣṭhaṃ sarvalokeśvareśvaram
english: Then, O great king, the son of Droṇa, his eyes brimming with tears and breathing hard, spoke to that foremost of the Bharatas, the lord of all the lords of the world.

sanskrit: na nūnaṃ vidyate 'sahyaṃ mānuṣye kiṃ cid eva hi yatra tvaṃ puruṣavyāghra śeṣe pāṃsuṣu rūṣitaḥ
english: Surely there is nothing unendurable in the lot of mortals, when you, O tiger among men, lie here smeared with dust.

sanskrit: bhūtvā hi nṛpatiḥ pūrvaṃ samājñāpya ca medinīm katham eko 'dya rājendra tiṣṭhase nirjane vane
english: Having once been a king, having ruled over the whole earth, how is it, O lord of kings, that today you lie alone in a desolate wood?

sanskrit: duḥśāsanaṃ na paśyāmi nāpi karṇaṃ mahāratham nāpi tān suhṛdaḥ sarvān kim idaṃ bharatarṣabha
english: I do not see Duḥśāsana, nor Karṇa the mighty charioteer, nor all those dear friends—what does this mean, O bull of the Bharatas?

sanskrit: duḥkhaṃ nūnaṃ kṛtāntasya gatiṃ jñātuṃ kathaṃ cana lokānāṃ ca bhavān yatra śete pāṃsuṣu rūṣitaḥ
english: Hard indeed it is, by any means, to know the course of fate, when you, the lord of the worlds, lie here smeared with dust.

sanskrit: eṣa mūrdhāvasiktānām agre gatvā paraṃtapaḥ satṛṇaṃ grasate pāṃsuṃ paśya kālasya paryayam
english: This scorcher of foes, who marched at the head of the anointed kings, now swallows dust along with grass—behold the reversal wrought by time!

sanskrit: kva te tad amalaṃ chatraṃ vyajanaṃ kva ca pārthiva sā ca te mahatī senā kva gatā pārthivottama
english: Where is that spotless parasol of yours, where the fan, O prince? Where has that mighty army of yours gone, O best of kings?

sanskrit: durvijñeyā gatir nūnaṃ kāryāṇāṃ kāraṇāntare yad vai lokagurur bhūtvā bhavān etāṃ daśāṃ gataḥ
english: Hard to fathom, surely, is the course of events when the cause is otherwise than it seems, for you, who were once the teacher of the world, have come to this pass.

sanskrit: adhruvā sarvamartyeṣu dhruvaṃ śrīr upalakṣyate bhavato vyasanaṃ dṛṣṭvā śakravispardhino bhṛśam
english: Among all mortals fortune is shown to be unstable indeed, now that we behold the grievous calamity of you who once rivalled Indra himself.

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā duḥkhitasya viśeṣataḥ uvāca rājan putras te prāptakālam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Hearing that speech of the deeply grieving man, O king, your son spoke these words befitting the hour.

sanskrit: vimṛjya netre pāṇibhyāṃ śokajaṃ bāṣpam utsṛjan kṛpādīn sa tadā vīrān sarvān eva narādhipaḥ
english: Wiping his eyes with both hands and shedding the tears born of sorrow, that ruler of men then addressed all those heroes, Kṛpa and the rest:

sanskrit: īdṛśo martyadharmo 'yaṃ dhātrā nirdiṣṭa ucyate vināśaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ kālaparyāyakāritaḥ
english: "Such, men say, is this law of mortals ordained by the Creator: the destruction of all beings, brought about by the turning of time.

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ māṃ samanuprāptaḥ pratyakṣaṃ bhavatāṃ hi yaḥ pṛthivīṃ pālayitvāham etāṃ niṣṭhām upāgataḥ
english: This destruction has now overtaken me before your very eyes—I who once protected the earth have come to this end.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā nāhaṃ parāvṛtto yuddhe kasyāṃ cid āpadi diṣṭyāhaṃ nihataḥ pāpaiś chalenaiva viśeṣataḥ
english: By good fortune I never turned my back in battle in any peril; by good fortune I have been slain by the wicked, and that especially through treachery.

sanskrit: utsāhaś ca kṛto nityaṃ mayā diṣṭyā yuyutsatā diṣṭyā cāsmi hato yuddhe nihatajñātibāndhavaḥ
english: By good fortune I, ever eager to fight, kept my resolve unflagging; by good fortune I am slain in battle, my kinsmen and friends already fallen.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā ca vo 'haṃ paśyāmi muktān asmāj janakṣayāt svastiyuktāṃś ca kalyāṃś ca tan me priyam anuttamam
english: And by good fortune I see you delivered from this slaughter of men, safe and sound and whole—that is to me a joy beyond all others.

sanskrit: mā bhavanto 'nutapyantāṃ sauhṛdān nidhanena me yadi vedāḥ pramāṇaṃ vo jitā lokā mayākṣayāḥ
english: Let none of you grieve out of affection at my death; if the Vedas are an authority for you, then the imperishable worlds have been won by me.

sanskrit: manyamānaḥ prabhāvaṃ ca kṛṣṇasyāmitatejasaḥ tena na cyāvitaś cāhaṃ kṣatradharmāt svanuṣṭhitāt
english: Though I knew well the might of Kṛṣṇa of boundless splendour, not even by him was I made to fall away from the warrior's law well observed.

sanskrit: sa mayā samanuprāpto nāsmi śocyaḥ kathaṃ cana kṛtaṃ bhavadbhiḥ sadṛśam anurūpam ivātmanaḥ yatitaṃ vijaye nityaṃ daivaṃ tu duratikramam
english: That end has been attained by me, and in no way am I to be mourned. You have acted in a manner worthy of yourselves and true to your nature; you strove ever for victory—but fate is hard to overcome."

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā vacanaṃ bāṣpavyākulalocanaḥ tūṣṇīṃ babhūva rājendra rujāsau vihvalo bhṛśam
english: Having spoken thus far, his eyes troubled with tears, he fell silent, O lord of kings, overwhelmed grievously by his pain.

sanskrit: tathā tu dṛṣṭvā rājānaṃ bāṣpaśokasamanvitam drauṇiḥ krodhena jajvāla yathā vahnir jagatkṣaye
english: But seeing the king thus filled with tears and grief, the son of Droṇa blazed up with wrath, like the fire at the dissolution of the world.

sanskrit: sa tu krodhasamāviṣṭaḥ pāṇau pāṇiṃ nipīḍya ca bāṣpavihvalayā vācā rājānam idam abravīt
english: And he, possessed by anger, wringing one hand within the other, spoke to the king in a voice broken by tears:

sanskrit: pitā me nihataḥ kṣudraiḥ sunṛśaṃsena karmaṇā na tathā tena tapyāmi yathā rājaṃs tvayādya vai
english: "My father was slain by base men through a most cruel deed; yet I do not grieve so much for that, O king, as I grieve this day for you.

sanskrit: śṛṇu cedaṃ vaco mahyaṃ satyena vadataḥ prabho iṣṭāpūrtena dānena dharmeṇa sukṛtena ca
english: Hear now this word of mine, O lord, as I speak in truth—by my sacrifices and works of merit, by my gifts, by my righteousness, and by my good deeds:

sanskrit: adyāhaṃ sarvapāñcālān vāsudevasya paśyataḥ sarvopāyair hi neṣyāmi pretarājaniveśanam anujñāṃ tu mahārāja bhavān me dātum arhati
english: This very day, before the eyes of Vāsudeva himself, I will by every means lead all the Pāñcālas to the dwelling-place of the king of the dead. But you, O great king, must grant me your leave."

sanskrit: iti śrutvā tu vacanaṃ droṇaputrasya kauravaḥ manasaḥ prītijananaṃ kṛpaṃ vacanam abravīt ācārya śīghraṃ kalaśaṃ jalapūrṇaṃ samānaya
english: Hearing this speech of Droṇa's son, which gladdened his heart, the Kaurava spoke this word to Kṛpa: "Teacher, bring quickly a pitcher filled with water."

sanskrit: sa tad vacanam ājñāya rājño brāhmaṇasattamaḥ kalaśaṃ pūrṇam ādāya rājño 'ntikam upāgamat
english: Understanding that command of the king, the best of brāhmaṇas took up a brimming pitcher and drew near to the king.

sanskrit: tam abravīn mahārāja putras tava viśāṃ pate mamājñayā dvijaśreṣṭha droṇaputro 'bhiṣicyatām senāpatyena bhadraṃ te mama ced icchasi priyam
english: Then your son spoke to him, O great king, O lord of peoples: "By my command, O foremost of the twice-born, let the son of Droṇa be consecrated to the office of commander-in-chief—blessings upon you—if you wish to do what pleases me."

sanskrit: rājño niyogād yoddhavyaṃ brāhmaṇena viśeṣataḥ vartatā kṣatradharmeṇa hy evaṃ dharmavido viduḥ
english: At the king's command a brāhmaṇa too must fight, and especially one who walks in the law of the warriors—so the knowers of dharma have declared.

sanskrit: rājñas tu vacanaṃ śrutvā kṛpaḥ śāradvatas tataḥ drauṇiṃ rājño niyogena senāpatye 'bhyaṣecayat
english: Hearing then the king's word, Kṛpa, the son of Śaradvat, by the king's command consecrated the son of Droṇa to the command of the army.

sanskrit: so 'bhiṣikto mahārāja pariṣvajya nṛpottamam prayayau siṃhanādena diśaḥ sarvā vinādayan
english: Once consecrated, O great king, he embraced that best of kings and set forth, making all the quarters resound with his lion's roar.

sanskrit: duryodhano 'pi rājendra śoṇitaughapariplutaḥ tāṃ niśāṃ pratipede 'tha sarvabhūtabhayāvahām
english: And Duryodhana too, O lord of kings, drenched in a flood of blood, then passed into that night which struck terror into all beings.

sanskrit: apakramya tu te tūrṇaṃ tasmād āyodhanān nṛpa śokasaṃvignamanasaś cintādhyānaparābhavan
english: Then, withdrawing swiftly from that field of battle, O king, their minds shaken with grief, they sank into the helplessness of brooding thought.
